  • lowerBound <= a < initial < b <= upperBound

  • a = lower and b = upper -- ConvergenceException
  • Integer.MAX_VALUE iterations elapse -- ConvergenceException

Find a real root in the given interval.

Original Muller's method would have function evaluation at complex point. Since our f op x cp is real we have to find ways to avoid that. Bracketing condition is one way to go: by requiring bracketing in every iteration the newly computed approximation is guaranteed to be real.

Normally Muller's method converges quadratically in the vicinity of a zero however it may be very slow in regions far away from zeros. For example f op x cp = exp op x cp - 1 min = -50 max = 100. In such case we use bisection as a safety backup if it performs very poorly.

Returns the LU decomposition as a BigMatrix. Returns a fresh copy of the cached LU matrix if this has been computed otherwise the composition is computed and cached for use by other methods. Since a copy is returned in either case changes to the returned matrix do not affect the LU decomposition property.

The matrix returned is a compact representation of the LU decomposition. Elements below the main diagonal correspond to entries of the ""L"" matrix elements on and above the main diagonal correspond to entries of the ""U"" matrix.

The L and U matrices satisfy the matrix equation LU = permuteRows op this cp
